info.title: FileSquid API
info.description: The single FileSquid API served by every FileSquid host. See resources/architecture/030-filesquid-api-and-transports.md. Conventions: a command (mutation) sends a CommandEnvelope as the `envelope` member of its JSON request body (operation_id is the idempotency key, expected_revision the revision last read) and answers with a CommandOutcome; a query (list) takes the PageSize (`limit`, 1-1000) and Cursor (`cursor`) parameters; every failed request answers with an ApiError body (code, message, retryable). Router-wide fallbacks: any /api/v1/ path not in this contract answers 404 not_found, and a documented path called with a method it does not document answers 405 method_not_allowed; both carry the ApiError body. They are not listed per operation because no operation sends them. Authorisation is deny-by-default: every operation, including health, the contract and the event channel, requires the bearerAuth credential and is authorised before anything else runs, so a call without it answers 401 unauthorized and a call whose credential is not accepted or does not grant the operation answers 403 forbidden, before any 404 or 405; both carry the ApiError body with a DenialReason in `reason`. Each operation names the authorisation action it performs in x-filesquid-action. The one deliberate exception is GET /api/v1/health/live (x-filesquid-action public, security []), a liveness probe that answers only {"status":"up"} without a credential. The content route GET and HEAD /api/v1/content/{handle} (x-filesquid-action content.read, x-filesquid-credential content-handle, security []) is not public: its only credential is the content handle in its path, minted by POST /api/v1/content-handles for one file version (API-S-018); a Bearer token is not accepted there, and every unusable request under /api/v1/content/ (unknown, malformed, missing, expired, evicted or revoked handle, an extra path segment or another method) answers one identical 403 forbidden with reason invalid_credentials, never 401, 404 or 405. Paths marked x-filesquid-host-route are served by the hosts, not by the filesquid-api router.

get.summary: Process health
Liveness probe: the process is up (public, no credential)
get.description: Deliberately public so process supervisors and load balancers can probe without a token. Answers only that the process is up: no version, no component detail, no journal. Full health is GET /api/v1/health, which needs the bearerAuth credential.

get.summary: This API contract
Host descriptor: host type, operator name and hosted backup and sync state
get.description: Which host this API runs on (host_type, supplied by the host when it starts, never derived from the request), who operates it (operator_name, a server's FILESQUID_OPERATOR_NAME; null on desktop and browser hosts and on an unnamed server) and the state of encrypted backup and sync to the ciphertext-only hosted service (hosted_service; backup and sync are reported separately because they are distinct guarantees). Every caller the host authenticates may read it (action host.read is granted to every accepted credential, not to administrators only); it is never public. A host.change event carries the whole new descriptor whenever a field changes; a client MUST read this route again after events.resync or a reconnect. A successful read is not journaled. The descriptor carries no token, content handle, key or key identifier, account or device identifier, e-mail address, quota, object count, size, timestamp, path or file name.

get.summary: Push events (WebSocket on filesquid-server; Tauri events named filesquid-event on filesquid-desktop).

101.description: Switching protocols to WebSocket. Each text frame is one ApiEvent.

get.description: One event channel for job progress and change notifications. Each event is an ApiEvent whose topic is an EventTopic; x-filesquid-event-payloads names the payload schema of each topic. Events are hints, not state: a client MUST NOT depend on receiving every event. A subscriber that falls more than 256 events behind, or whose next event encodes to more than 65536 bytes, receives one events.resync event (EventResync) instead of the events it missed and MUST reread the state it shows through the request routes; a client that reconnects MUST do the same. At most 64 subscribers are served at once. Authorisation: send Authorization: Bearer <token>; a browser, which cannot set headers on a WebSocket, offers the subprotocols filesquid.events.v1 and filesquid.bearer.<token> instead, and the server selects filesquid.events.v1. A refused upgrade answers 401 or 403 with an ApiError body instead of switching protocols.

get.summary: List one folder of an object version, by path or by navigation node
get.description: The folders and files directly below a logical-path prefix, folders first, with an opaque cursor; limit 1-1000, default 200. The folder is named either by library_id and object_id with an optional prefix, or by one collection or folder navigation node (API-S-021), never both (400 invalid_request otherwise). A node must be readable to the caller: an unknown, malformed or unreadable node, or one no object holds, answers one identical 404 not_found; a library, virtual collection or repository node answers 400 invalid_request. The reserved folders provenance (PROV-O records) and .filesquid (application data) are left out of the root's page, so a page may hold fewer entries than asked while next_cursor remains; a prefix inside them answers 404. Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

parameters.name: library_id
parameters.description: The library; given with object_id, never with node.

parameters.name: object_id
parameters.description: The OCFL object; given with library_id, never with node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: A collection or folder node handle, as the navigation listing gave it (clients never parse it), instead of library_id, object_id and prefix.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The folder, a logical-path prefix without a trailing /; the root when absent.

get.summary: Download one whole file version, streamed
get.description: The whole file of any size as an attachment, streamed from ranged reads of at most 8 MiB so the host never holds the file in memory (NFR-003). A missing file is refused before the answer starts; a storage failure after it started ends the stream early and is journaled once. Through the desktop scheme every answer is capped at 16 MiB (DE-S-005), so the desktop UI saves larger files with ranged reads of GET /api/v1/files/content. A successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

Content-Disposition.description: attachment, naming the file by its display name: an ASCII filename fallback and the display name as RFC 5987 filename* UTF-8 (RFC 6266).

get.summary: Storage facts about one file
get.description: Object identifier, logical path, digest, size, fixity values, the version that last set the content and the media type; never the OCFL content path. Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

get.summary: The versions that changed one file
get.description: Oldest first; versions that left the file as it was are not listed. Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

get.summary: Every version of an object
get.description: Oldest first, with the head. Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

get.summary: Ranged read of one file version
get.description: One Range per request; each answer carries at most 16 MiB (the desktop scheme's buffer cap, DE-S-005). Media elements, which cannot send Authorization, read through a content handle instead (POST /api/v1/content-handles). Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

With a `Range` header it answers the status and headers the GET for that range answers (`206` with `Content-Range`, or `416` with `bytes */<length>`); without one it describes the whole file, so the client learns its length.

put.description: The body is the file's bytes, at most 64 MiB. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the filesquid-ocfl change model, or is refused (409) without publishing when nothing would change, another change is staged or the head is incomplete (API-S-008). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The version message, 1 to 1,024 bytes and not blank.

post.summary: Create a folder (pending until a file is added)
post.description: Writes nothing: OCFL stores no empty folder, so a new folder stays pending in the client and is persisted only when a file is added beneath its prefix. A file at the path or at a parent of it is a conflict.

200.description: Whether the folder exists or stays pending.

post.summary: Move or rename one file or folder
post.description: A folder moves every file below it; no bytes are written. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the filesquid-ocfl change model, or is refused (409) without publishing when nothing would change, another change is staged or the head is incomplete (API-S-008). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

The bytes stay in the object for history and restore. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the filesquid-ocfl change model, or is refused (409) without publishing when nothing would change, another change is staged or the head is incomplete (API-S-008). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

post.summary: Restore files or folders from an earlier version
post.description: One restore operation (API-S-014): the new version points at the content the earlier version holds, a revert when it returns every file of the object to that version's and the head holds no other, else a reinstate, named so in the version's filesquid.operation.v1 message, which carries the optional label. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the filesquid-ocfl change model and leaves earlier versions untouched, or is refused (409) without publishing when nothing would change, another change is staged or the head is incomplete (API-S-008). Paths in the reserved .filesquid folder are refused (400). With provenance configured the version carries its PROV-O record (API-S-028). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

post.summary: Mint a content handle for one file version
post.description: For media elements (img, video, audio, source), which cannot send Authorization (API-S-018, ADR 030 Decision 5). Authorised exactly like the ranged read of that file version (action files.read; a refusal is the refusal that read gets); a content handle cannot mint another. The handle is 256 bits from the operating system's CSPRNG; the API keeps only its SHA-256 digest, in memory. At most 1,024 live handles per credential: another mint evicts the least recently used one. Journaled as api.content_handle.issued (actor, library, object, version and expiry; never the handle).

200.description: The handle, its URL and its absolute expiry.

get.summary: Read one file version through a content handle
get.description: Serves only the file version the handle names, with the ranged read's single-range handling and 16 MiB cap. The handle is accepted at the start of each request: 300 s after its mint or last accepted request, or 3,600 s after its mint, or once its minting credential ends or may no longer read files, it is refused; an answer that has started is never cut off. Every answer, denials included, carries Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cache-Control: private, no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox.

parameters.description: The content handle: this route's only credential. Never logged, journaled or echoed; hosts that record request paths record /api/v1/content/{handle}.

get.summary: Open OCFL validation findings and validation runs
get.description: API-S-022. The open findings of every open library (at most 1,000, ordered by library, object, code and location; `truncated` when more are open) the schedule and cap in force and, per open library, whether a run is going, the last run and the next scheduled run. A finding's `location` is null for a caller who may not read the object: the server administrator, until per-object permissions arrive.

post.description: API-S-022. Starts a validation run of the named library, or of every open library when the body is empty or names none. A run continues from the library's stored cursor unless `from_start` is true. Runs go in the background and report in the process registry (`ocfl.validation`) and on the event channel. Starting a job changes no library content or organisation, so the body is a RunRequest, not a CommandEnvelope. Every refusal is journaled as `ocfl.validation.run`.

200.description: The libraries whose run started, and those refused.

404.description: The named library is not open on this host (`not_found`).

409.description: A run of the named library is already going (`already_running`).

put.summary: Change the OCFL validation schedule and cap
put.description: API-S-022. The desktop owner or a server administrator changes the time between scheduled runs and the object cap of a run. The next scheduled run of each open library moves with the new interval. Answers the settings now in force. Changing settings changes no library content or organisation, so the body is the settings, not a CommandEnvelope. Every change and refusal is journaled as `ocfl.validation.configure`.

post.description: API-S-029. The desktop owner or a server administrator starts one backfill over every OCFL storage root the host serves, in the background, and the route answers 200 at once. Each run registers in the process registry (`prov.backfill`), checkpoints per object, stops at its cap or on cancel (the host's exit), skips versions that already have a record, and commits one provenance-only version per object. The request carries no body. A request while a backfill runs is refused 409 conflict. The request is journaled once as `history.backfill.request` (succeeded, or failed with its error code: `backfill_running`, `unavailable`); each run journals itself. Starting a job changes no library content or organisation, so there is no CommandEnvelope.

200.description: The backfill started in the background.

409.description: A history backfill is already running (`conflict`).

get.summary: List one level of the navigation tree
get.description: One level of the tree a UI shows as its navigation and breadcrumb (API-S-021). Without node: the host's one repository. With node: that node's children - a repository's libraries; a library's collections, then its virtual collections, then the folders its unfiled files imply; a collection's folders; a folder's subfolders; nothing under a virtual collection; never files. A folder exists only when committed ordinary files imply it, so one implied only by hidden or deleted files is not listed. Every node carries an opaque handle (at most 512 bytes, never a path, storage key, SQL or token), its kind, its name and has_children (true only when the caller may read a child). ancestors holds the nodes from the repository down to and including the listed node, for the breadcrumb. Paging: limit 1-1000 (default 200) and an opaque cursor, in a stable order - the fixed kind order library, collection, virtual_collection, folder; libraries, collections and virtual collections in catalog order; folders by name in Unicode code-point order; no repeat or gap across pages. A page may hold fewer nodes than limit while next_cursor is present (nodes the caller may not read are skipped); keep following next_cursor until it is null. Only nodes the caller may read are listed, counted or named in an ancestor trail; an unknown node and one the caller may not read, or one under an unreadable ancestor, get the same 404 not_found. A folder whose handle would exceed 512 bytes cannot be named and is not listed. A malformed cursor, a cursor of another level, a limit outside 1-1000 or an unknown parameter answers 400 invalid_request. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once as navigation.list (API-S-017). Subscribe to navigation.change on the event channel to know when to read a level again.

200.description: One page of one level of the tree.

post.summary: Create a library in an empty folder
post.description: Makes the folder the host registered as location_id the OCFL 1.1 storage root of a library: writes only the 0=ocfl_1.1 declaration, never over an existing file, and needs no account or connection (F-001). Answers the library ID (library_id when given, else a new UUID v4), which stays bound to the location until the host stops. Refusals: invalid_location, invalid_library, location_not_found, location_in_use, library_already_open, too_many_libraries (at most 64 open libraries) and root_not_empty. The outcome is journaled as library.root.create. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

post.summary: Open the library in a folder
post.description: Opens the OCFL storage root in the folder the host registered as location_id through the engine's guards, and binds the library ID (library_id when given, else a new UUID v4) to it. Writes and repairs nothing. Opening a location that is already open answers its library again. Refusals: invalid_location, invalid_library, location_not_found, location_in_use, library_already_open, too_many_libraries, not_a_storage_root and git_in_root. Only a failure is journaled, as library.root.open. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

post.summary: Copy a completed snapshot to an empty folder
post.description: Copies the committed files of every object of the open library into the empty folder the host registered as destination_location_id, never over an existing file, and validates the copy, so it is a checked OCFL root ordinary tools can read (F-042). The library is only read. Refusals: library_not_open, location_not_found, destination_overlaps_library (the destination is the folder of an open library, or inside or around one), destination_not_empty, snapshot_unreadable and snapshot_incomplete (retryable while a head is being published). The outcome is journaled as library.snapshot.copy. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: What the copy wrote and what its validation found.

post.summary: Rebuild a library from its files
post.description: Reads every object of the open library from its OCFL files alone, so a host can rebuild its catalog without its database. Validation errors are reported, never adopted or repaired, and an object whose head has no version inventory is flagged. Writes nothing. Refusals: library_not_open and the open errors of the storage root. The outcome is journaled as library.rebuild. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

get.summary: Objects whose head has no version inventory
get.description: The objects of the open library whose committed head lacks its version inventory or its sidecar (W010): what the UI may offer to repair, at most 1,000 (OCFL-S-020, API-S-023). Writes and repairs nothing. Refusals: library_not_open and the open errors of the storage root. Only a failure is journaled, as library.repair_candidates. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

post.summary: Repair the version inventory of named objects, with the owner's consent
post.description: The one command that adds a file to an existing version directory: for each named object whose committed head has no version inventory, adds one copy of the root inventory and its sidecar to the head version directory and changes nothing else (OCFL-S-020, API-S-023). Only a library's owner may run it: the desktop owner; on filesquid-server every caller, the administrator included, is refused 403 not_permitted until server accounts give a library owner a principal. The request names the library and 1 to 1,000 distinct objects and carries the owner's consent to statement version_inventory_repair.v1 for exactly those objects; without it the request is refused (consent_required, consent_mismatch) and nothing is written. Each object gets its own outcome in the answer: an object whose head already holds its version inventory and sidecar is refused nothing_to_repair, never repaired. The consent and each object's outcome are journaled as ocfl.repair.version_inventory (opaque IDs, version, outcome, error code). Refusals of the whole request: invalid_objects, consent_required, consent_mismatch, library_not_open and the open errors of the storage root. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: One outcome per requested object, in request order.

put.summary: Set or clear the label of one version after commit
put.description: Commits one version (operation kind label) holding the object's application-data file .filesquid/labels.json, which maps labelled versions to their later labels; null clears a commit-time label. That version's own message carries no label. The file is recovered with the object from an ordinary copy. At most 1,000 labelled versions per object. A label that would not change what the version shows is refused (409) without publishing. Labels never affect retention. With provenance configured the version carries its PROV-O record (API-S-028). Journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

get.summary: The bytes one file's history keeps
get.description: The versions that changed the file, its distinct contents and their bytes, each content counted once (SRS-F-065). A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

get.summary: The bytes a library's history keeps
get.description: Every object's distinct contents and their bytes, each content of an object counted once, within 10,000 objects and 100,000 contents (truncated says when a bound stopped the count). Nothing is deleted, expired or thinned to free space. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

post.summary: Journal the UI's console warnings and errors
post.description: API-S-030. At most 20 events and 16 KiB per request; each event becomes its own journal entry (ui.console.warn, ui.console.error or ui.console.overflow), journaled once per client event ID, and the batch is acknowledged only after the entries are stored. 60 requests a minute per credential, refused requests included; a request that carries only one overflow event naming no other principal is exempt. An event naming another principal than the credential's is refused (403, journaled).

200.description: Every event of the batch is journaled.

get.summary: Read the caller's UI preferences
get.description: The caller's own saved preferences (API-S-011, SRS-F-062), or the defaults when they saved none. A successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

put.description: Replace the caller's own preferences with a complete, checked value: every field, schema 1, navigation version 1, at most 100 pinned node handles, 16 section ids of 1 to 64 characters and 1,000 collapsed node handles, each once (UI-S-017). Node entries must be handles the navigation listing wrote; no name, title, logical path, token or content handle is stored. Each pin's kind must be the kind its handle names. A host that keeps preferences for no more users answers 409 conflict (not retryable). A save is journaled once as preferences.update with the actor only, never the values.

ApiEvent.description: One push event on the event channel: a topic and that topic's payload.

EventTopic.description: Documented event topics: process.update (a process or job changed), journal.entry (an activity journal entry was written), health.change (the health status changed), events.resync (events were missed; reread state), host.change (a host descriptor field changed; the payload is the whole new HostDescriptor; reread GET /api/v1/host after events.resync or a reconnect), navigation.change (children of navigation nodes changed; the payload is a NavigationChange; read the named parents' levels of GET /api/v1/navigation again, or the whole visible tree on all, events.resync or a reconnect).

missed.description: How many events this subscriber did not receive.

EventResync.description: Payload of events.resync: the subscriber missed events and MUST reread the state it shows.

operation_id.description: Opaque operation ID shared by every entry and OCFL version of one operation (ADR 040).

object_ref.description: OCFL object version the entry is about: `<object-id>@vN`.

client_event_id.description: Client event ID (UUID v4) of an entry recorded from POST /api/v1/client-events; journaled at most once (API-S-030).

codes.description: Machine-readable codes behind the reason, when it has any: for ocfl_validation_errors, the OCFL error codes of the open findings, sorted. Absent otherwise.

objects.description: How many objects the reason concerns (ocfl_validation_errors). Absent otherwise.

journal_unsealed_age_ms.description: How long the oldest entry a seal left unsealed has waited, in milliseconds; null when the last seals left none or the host seals nothing (API-S-032). Over two sealing intervals (2 hours) it raises the journal_unsealed reason.

Liveness.description: Body of the public liveness probe. Says only that the process is up.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error code. HTTP status: invalid_request 400, unauthorized 401, forbidden 403, not_found 404, method_not_allowed 405, conflict 409, payload_too_large 413, range_not_satisfiable 416, rate_limited 429, internal 500, unavailable 503. Only unavailable and rate_limited are retryable (rate_limited once Retry-After has passed). The router-wide fallbacks use 404 not_found (path not in the contract) and 405 method_not_allowed (method not documented for the path). A 416 range_not_satisfiable answer also carries Content-Range: bytes */<length>; a 429 rate_limited answer carries Retry-After.

DenialReason.description: Why the authorisation layer refused a call: missing_credentials (401 unauthorized), invalid_credentials (403 forbidden: the credential is not accepted by this host) or not_permitted (403 forbidden: the caller is known but may not perform this operation). Never retryable.

ApiError.description: Body of every failed API request. Authorisation denials (401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden) also carry `reason`.

message.description: Human-readable message the UI can show. Never contains paths, SQL or internal error text.

retryable.description: True when repeating the same request unchanged may succeed.

PortError.description: Error reported by a module port, with retryability (CORE-S-005).

operation_id.description: Operation and idempotency key: repeating a command with the same id MUST NOT apply it twice.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read; a mismatch answers conflict.

CommandOutcomeKind.description: committed is durable completion evidence; pending is durable but incomplete; conflict means the expected revision did not match; error carries a PortError.

CommandOutcome.description: Result of a command, tied to its operation id.

error.description: The module error when kind is error, otherwise null.

HostType.description: The kind of host the API runs on, supplied by the host itself: desktop (filesquid-desktop), server (filesquid-server, whose operator can read what it stores) or browser (the encrypted browser host).

HostedService.description: Encrypted backup and sync to the ciphertext-only hosted service. When enrolled is false, backup_enabled and sync_enabled are false and service_host is null. When enrolled is true, service_host is the service's lowercase DNS host name (no scheme, port, path, user information or query) and backup_enabled and sync_enabled are reported separately.

service_host.description: Lowercase DNS host name of the hosted service, or null when not enrolled.

HostDescriptor.description: The answer of GET /api/v1/host and the payload of a host.change event.

operator_name.description: The server operator's display name (trimmed, 1 to 256 characters, no control characters); null on desktop and browser hosts and on a server without FILESQUID_OPERATOR_NAME.

OperationKind.description: The kind of a committed operation: one activity of the PROV-O history.

JournalLink.description: The journal entries of one committed operation.

HistoryEntry.description: One activity of the history as the API and UI show it (API-S-029). Agents are opaque identifiers, never a person identity.

started_at.description: When the operation started; null for a reconstructed record.

ended_at.description: When the version was committed (the inventory created time).

reconstructed.description: Whether the record was reconstructed from the inventory afterwards.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

truncated.description: True when the history index stopped at its record or object cap (100 000 each) or skipped an object it could not open, so this page may miss activities.

VersionUser.description: Who made a version, as the OCFL inventory records it.

address.description: A URI for the user, when recorded.

VersionRecord.description: One version of an OCFL object.

created.description: When it was created, RFC 3339 as recorded.

message.description: Why it was made, when recorded.

label.description: The version's label (PRD F-065): the later label when one was set (PUT /api/v1/files/labels), else the label member of its filesquid.operation.v1 message; null when it has none. Labels never affect retention. Always sent; optional in the schema so clients written before labels still read it.

FolderEntry.description: One entry of a folder listing: a folder or a file, told apart by kind.

anyOf.description: A folder implied by the logical paths below it (OCFL stores no empty folder).

name.description: Its last path segment: the name it is stored under.

display_name.description: The name users see: the owner's original file name from the host's file record, made safe (no path separator or control character), or the stored name when no record holds one. Users never see the stored name in its place.

digest.description: Its content digest (the inventory's digest algorithm).

modified_version.description: The version that last set its content.

modified.description: When that version was created, RFC 3339.

type_hint.description: The lowercase extension: a display hint only, never a format identification.

FolderPage.description: One page of a folder listing: folders first, then files, at most the requested limit (1-1000, default 200).

prefix.description: The folder listed, a logical-path prefix without a trailing /; empty for the root.

next_cursor.description: The opaque cursor of the next page, or null on the last page.

FileDetails.description: Storage facts about one file of one version. The OCFL content path, storage keys and filesystem paths are never answered (API-S-005).

name.description: Its last path segment: the name it is stored under.

display_name.description: The name users see: the owner's original file name from the host's file record, made safe (no path separator or control character), or the stored name when no record holds one. Users never see the stored name in its place.

digest_algorithm.description: The digest algorithm: sha512 or sha256.

fixity.description: Fixity values the inventory records for its content, by algorithm.

type_hint.description: The lowercase extension: a display hint only.

media_type.description: The media type content answers carry, from the extension until the file record of MD-0.8 stores the type given at import; never sniffed.

FileChange.description: How a version changed one file.

FileHistoryEntry.description: One version that changed a file.

digest.description: The file's digest after the change, or null when it was removed.

size.description: The file's size in bytes after the change, or null when it was removed. Always sent; optional in the schema so clients written before sizes still read it.

FileHistory.description: The versions that changed one file, oldest first.

ObjectVersions.description: Every version of an OCFL object, oldest first.

FileCommit.description: The one OCFL version a write published (API-S-008).

created.description: When it was created, RFC 3339 UTC.

FolderAnswer.description: The answer to creating a folder. Nothing is written: OCFL stores no empty folder.

pending.description: True when no file lies below the folder yet, so it exists only in the client until a file is added beneath it; false when it already exists.

MoveRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/files/moves: move or rename one file or folder (every file below it) in one new version.

from.description: The file or folder to move.

message.description: The version message, 1 to 1,024 bytes and not blank.

RemoveRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/files/removals: remove one file or folder in one new version; its bytes stay in the object for history and restore.

path.description: The file or folder to remove.

message.description: The version message, 1 to 1,024 bytes and not blank.

RestoreRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/files/restorations: restore files or folders to their content in an earlier version, in one new version.

paths.description: The files or folders to restore, 1 to 1,000.

label.description: The new version's label: 1 to 512 bytes, not blank, no control characters. It is the label member of the version's filesquid.operation.v1 message; a restore takes no free message.

ContentHandleRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/content-handles: exactly one file object, OCFL version and logical path.

version.description: The one version the handle reads: v1, v2, ... (head is not accepted).

path.description: The file's logical path in that version.

ContentHandle.description: A content handle for media elements (API-S-018): the handle is answered here and nowhere else, and never logged or journaled.

handle.description: The handle: 256 random bits as 43 base64url characters without padding.

url.description: Its relative URL, /api/v1/content/<handle>, for a media element's src.

expires_at.description: Its absolute expiry, RFC 3339 UTC: 3,600 s after the mint. It also ends after 300 s without a request, and when the credential that minted it ends.

location.description: Storage key (and JSON pointer) of the fault; null for a caller who may not read the object.

library_id.description: The one library to run; every open library when absent or null.

from_start.description: Start at the beginning of the object order instead of the stored cursor (default false).

interval_ms.description: Time between scheduled runs of a library, in milliseconds (one hour to 366 days; default 7 days).

NavigationKind.description: What a navigation node stands for. A listing orders children by this fixed order (library, collection, virtual_collection, folder); a client never sorts by the names.

NavigationNode.description: One node of the navigation tree.

node.description: The opaque handle. Clients MUST NOT parse it; it holds no filesystem path, storage key, OCFL content path, SQL or token.

name.description: The title of a library, collection or virtual collection; the last segment of a folder's logical path; for a repository, the name its host is configured with, or null (the UI then uses its own label).

has_children.description: True only when the caller may read at least one child of the node. A virtual collection never has children here.

NavigationPage.description: One page of one level of the navigation tree (API-S-021).

nodes.description: The nodes of this page, in the stable order of the listing.

ancestors.description: For a listed node: the nodes from the repository down to and including that node, so one call fills a breadcrumb. Empty at the repository level.

next_cursor.description: The opaque cursor of the next page, or null on the last page.

NavigationChange.description: Payload of navigation.change: after a committed change adds, removes, renames or moves a node, the nodes whose children changed. Exactly one of parents (1 to 64 handles) and all is present. A subscriber receives only the handles it may read and no event when it may read none.

parents.description: The handles (1 to 64) of the nodes whose children changed; read those levels again.

all.description: True when more than 64 changed or the changed parents are not known; read the whole visible tree again.

LibraryLocationRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/libraries and POST /api/v1/libraries/openings: the folder the owner chose, by the opaque location ID the host registered it under, never by its path.

location_id.description: The opaque location ID, 1 to 128 bytes.

library_id.description: The library ID to use, at most 128 bytes; a new UUID v4 when absent.
The library, bound to the location until the host stops.

spec_version.description: The OCFL version the storage root declares (1.1).

library_id.description: The library: an opaque ID, at most 128 bytes.

destination_location_id.description: The opaque location ID of the empty folder to copy into, 1 to 128 bytes.

LibraryRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/libraries/rebuilds: the open library.

library_id.description: The library: an opaque ID, at most 128 bytes.

ObjectFindings.description: An object of a snapshot copy whose validation found errors.

error_codes.description: The distinct OCFL validation codes of its errors (E###), sorted.

SnapshotCopyReport.description: What a snapshot copy wrote and what its validation found.

invalid_objects.description: Copied objects whose validation found errors; empty for a clean copy.

RebuiltObject.description: One object rebuilt from its files.

files.description: Logical files in the head version.

digest_algorithm.description: The object's digest algorithm (sha256 or sha512).

error_codes.description: Distinct OCFL validation error codes (E###), sorted; empty for a valid object.

missing_version_inventory.description: Whether the head lacks its version inventory or its sidecar: a candidate for the consented repair.

UnreadableObject.description: An object a rebuild could not open; its location is not reported.

error_code.description: The OCFL validation code when an OCFL rule is broken (E###), else unreadable.

RebuildReport.description: Everything a rebuild from files found.

unreadable.description: Objects that could not be opened.

RepairCandidate.description: An object the UI may offer to repair.

head.description: The committed head version that lacks its version inventory.

digest_algorithm.description: The object's digest algorithm (sha256 or sha512).

interrupted.description: True when the head already holds its version inventory but not its sidecar: an interrupted repair the command completes.

committable_after_repair.description: True for sha256 objects; a sha512 object stays readable-only after the repair.

candidates.description: Candidates in object-root order, at most 1,000.

truncated.description: True when more candidates exist than were answered.

RepairConsent.description: The owner's consent from the repair dialog: the library and exactly the objects it named, and the statement it showed.

object_ids.description: The objects the dialog named: exactly those of the request.

statement_id.description: The statement shown: version_inventory_repair.v1. A consent to other words is refused.

confirmed.description: True only when the owner confirmed; cancelling sends no request.

object_ids.description: The objects to repair: 1 to 1,000 distinct identifiers, each at most 1,024 bytes.

consent.description: The owner's consent; a request without a confirmed consent is refused.

version.description: The head version, when the object was found.

error_code.description: Why it was refused (for example nothing_to_repair, object_not_found, reservation_held); null when repaired.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed later.

provenance_version.description: The provenance-only version that records a repaired object, when it was committed.

provenance_error_code.description: Why a repaired object's provenance record was not written, when it was not.

RepairAnswer.description: The answer to a repair command.

run_id.description: The repair run: the operation ID its consent and outcome entries share, an opaque UUID v4.

LabelRequest.description: Body of PUT /api/v1/files/labels: set or clear the label of one version after commit.

version.description: The version to label: v1, v2, ...

label.description: The label: 1 to 512 bytes, not blank, no control characters; null or absent clears it.

FileHistorySize.description: The bytes one file's history keeps: each distinct content once.

versions.description: The versions that changed the file.

contents.description: The distinct contents the file has had.

bytes.description: Their bytes, each content counted once.

LibraryHistorySize.description: The bytes a library's history keeps: each distinct content of each object once, within 10,000 objects and 100,000 contents.

bytes.description: Their bytes, each content of an object counted once.

truncated.description: True when a bound stopped the count, so the totals are lower bounds.

ProvenanceLink.description: Where the PROV-O activity of an entry's operation is (API-S-031). Entries of committed operations (outcome succeeded, with operation_id and object_ref) link to it; failed and refused entries, entries without both identifiers and file.download entries are journal_only.

journal_only.description: True when the entry has no PROV-O activity.

operation_id.description: The operation ID the activity carries.

object_ref.description: The object version the activity is about: `<object-id>@vN`.

record.description: API path of the version's PROV-O record (GET /api/v1/files/{id}/versions/{version}/prov), for a urn:uuid object.

activities.description: API path of every activity of the operation (GET /api/v1/history?operation=...).

operation_id.description: Opaque operation ID shared by every entry and OCFL version of one operation (ADR 040).

object_ref.description: OCFL object version the entry is about: `<object-id>@vN`.

client_event_id.description: Client event ID (UUID v4) of an entry recorded from POST /api/v1/client-events; journaled at most once (API-S-030).

display_name.description: Current display name of the file the entry's object ID names, resolved at read time for the caller.

JournalEntryView.description: A journal entry as the journal routes answer it: the stored entry, its PROV-O link and, only with names=true and only when the host resolves it for the caller, the current display name of the file its object ID names (display only; never stored or exported).

ClientConsoleEvent.description: A console warning or error (API-S-030). Only these fields are read; any other field (a message, URL, file name or stack) is ignored and never stored.

id.description: Client event ID, a UUID v4 the event keeps for life.

component.description: Fixed identifier of the UI component, an opaque token.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code, an opaque token.

ids.description: At most 8 opaque IDs of what the event concerns.

time.description: When the event was raised (RFC 3339), at most five minutes ahead of the host's clock; the host's time when absent.

principal.description: The opaque principal that raised the event, as the client stored it; refused (403) when it differs from the credential's.

ClientOverflowEvent.description: The page-close count of events the client could not keep because IndexedDB was unavailable or refused a write (API-S-030, the one recorded gap). No other field is accepted.

id.description: Client event ID, a UUID v4.

ClientEventsRequest.description: 1 to 20 events in a body of at most 16 KiB.

acknowledged.description: Every client event ID of the batch, in request order without repeats; each is journaled now or was before.

journaled.description: Entries this request added (IDs already journaled add none).

principal.description: The credential's opaque principal, which the client stores with the events it keeps.

PinnedDestination.description: One pinned destination: its node handle and kind, never its name (UI-S-017).

NavigationPreferences.description: The navigation tree's pinned destinations, section order and collapsed nodes (UI-S-017). pinned, order and collapsed may be left out on PUT, meaning empty.

pinned.description: At most 100 pinned destinations, each node once.

order.description: At most 16 section ids in the user's order, each once.

collapsed.description: At most 1,000 collapsed node handles, each once.

Preferences.description: One user's UI preferences (API-S-011, SRS-F-062): choices only, never a name, title, logical path, token or content handle.

hover_card.description: Whether hovering an item shows its card. Default true.

StartView.description: Where the UI opens: Home or the root of the user's personal library. Default home.

SortKey.description: What listings are sorted by. Default name.

FolderPlacement.description: Folders before files, or sorted among them. Default on_top.

Layout.description: How listings are laid out. Default list.

BackfillStarted.description: A history backfill that started in the background (API-S-029). Its runs appear in the process registry and the journal as `prov.backfill`.

PageSize.name: limit
PageSize.description: Page size for a query (1-1000). Each operation states its default; the activity journal defaults to 100.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

Version.name: version
Version.description: The version: head (the default) or one such as v1.

Range.name: Range
Range.description: One byte range: bytes=a-b, bytes=a- or bytes=-n. A malformed header, another unit or several ranges are ignored.

NavigationNode.name: node
NavigationNode.description: The opaque handle of the node whose children to list, as an earlier answer gave it (clients never parse it). Absent: the host's repository level. An unknown, malformed or unreadable handle answers one identical 404 not_found.

Unauthorized.description: No credentials were presented (unauthorized, reason missing_credentials).

Forbidden.description: The credentials are not accepted (reason invalid_credentials) or do not permit this operation (reason not_permitted).

HostNotDescribed.description: The host has not described itself yet (unavailable; retryable).

NotFound.description: Nothing is recorded there, or the library, object, version, folder or file does not exist (not_found). One answer for all of them.

HistoryUnavailable.description: The host has not installed its history source yet, or its storage cannot be read now (unavailable; retryable).

Conflict.description: The write would change nothing, another change is staged, the object changed at the same paths meanwhile, a file has that path, or the head is incomplete (conflict); nothing was published.

RangeNotSatisfiable.description: The range starts at or past the end of the file (range_not_satisfiable). Carries Content-Range: bytes */<length>.

FilesUnavailable.description: The library's storage is not reachable, or the host has not installed its file service yet (unavailable; retryable).

ContentDenied.description: The one identical denial of the content route (forbidden, reason invalid_credentials, not retryable) for any unusable handle: unknown, malformed, missing, expired, evicted, revoked, or one whose minting credential no longer may read files. Same status, headers and body every time; a HEAD denial has no body. No file is read first.

LibraryNotFound.description: The location ID is not one the host registered (location_not_found), or the library is not open on this host (library_not_open) (not_found). The answer's code is not_found; the journal entry names which.

LibraryConflict.description: Refused by a rule about the storage root, the destination or the consent (conflict); nothing was written. The journal entry names the rule: root_not_empty, not_a_storage_root, git_in_root, destination_not_empty, snapshot_unreadable, destination_overlaps_library, location_in_use, library_already_open, too_many_libraries, consent_required or consent_mismatch.

LibraryUnavailable.description: The library's storage, the repair ledger or the reservation store is not reachable now, a head is still being published (snapshot_incomplete), or the host has not installed its library commands yet (unavailable; retryable).

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is larger than the route accepts (payload_too_large).

RateLimited.description: Over the route's rate bound (rate_limited). Retry after Retry-After seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until a request is admitted again.

PreferencesUnavailable.description: The host keeps no preferences yet, or their store cannot be reached (unavailable; retryable).

bearerAuth.description: Deny-by-default credential required by every operation. filesquid-desktop: the per-launch token the host generates at every launch and gives only to its own webviews (window.__FILESQUID_LAUNCH_TOKEN__). filesquid-server: the administrator token (FILESQUID_ADMIN_TOKEN or <data dir>/admin-token) until accounts, sessions and groups arrive. A WebSocket upgrade may carry it as the subprotocol filesquid.bearer.<token>.
